title: Edit is one glyph across the corpus: ic-pencil, not ic-pen
goal: The Edit action shows a pencil on some pages and a pen nib on fifty others, and the pen nib already means the vector drawing tool. This makes Edit a pencil everywhere so one picture keeps one meaning.
notes: DONE. ic-pencil is the edit verb everywhere; ic-pen is vector only. 206 replacements in 58 pages + shared/components/entry.js; shared/dist rebuilt via node shared/build-ds.mjs. Rule recorded in shared/AGENTS.md under Iconography ("One picture, one meaning"). Verification was browser-side: match BOTH [title="Edit"] and [data-tip="Edit"] because the tooltip component rewrites title at runtime. Known borrowed glyph: pages/export-share.html spec panel uses ic-document for its CSS section header because shared/icons.mjs has no code glyph - add one if a code block ever needs a real icon. Left as vector on purpose: layers-pane/icon-draw-wt arrow layer rows and redline.html "Arrow / annotate (P)", filed separately.
acceptance: Every Edit control across the study shows the pencil icon, including ones added automatically to generated cards
The pen nib icon appears only for the vector pen tool
A browser spot check of an item's action row shows the pencil, and the automated page sweep is clean

log.note: Adversarial review of the premise, before touching anything. The task notes proposed a blind text replace of title="Edit"><i class="ic ic-pen". That is right for the bulk but wrong as the whole job: of 304 ic-pen occurrences in the study, 179 are the Edit button, and the remaining 125 split into real vector uses (73 Pen tool controls, 29 Pen menu items, 10 vector layer rows, 4 text-on-a-path, 1 SVG export) and 27 MORE edit-verb uses the proposed pattern would have missed entirely. Classified every occurrence by its enclosing control rather than by string.

Findings the notes missed: 13 filmcard action rows say title="Open" instead of "Edit" on the IDENTICAL component the exemplar (app-shell.html History sheet) labels "Edit" - same verb, two spellings, both wearing the nib. 4 dsys.html Rename buttons and 1 ds-build-wt Rename button (icons.mjs describes pencil as "Edit, rename, freehand line", and dashboard.html already uses pencil for Rename). 2 primary [nib] Open buttons on capture cards (capture-wt, video-entry-wt). dsys "Edit main". export-share share-access Edit chip AND its JS ACCESS map, where the comment level also borrowed the nib. 2 video-title-wt editable-value carets. 1 export-share CSS section header, where the nib meant neither edit nor vector.

Judgment calls, recorded rather than guessed silently. (a) The 13 title="Open" filmcard buttons were retitled to "Edit" as well as re-glyphed: leaving "Open" on a pencil would have swapped one mismatch for another, and the exemplar component says Edit. (b) The 2 labelled primary "Open" buttons kept their visible word (that copy is correct for what they do) and took the pencil, since opening a capture is opening it to edit it. (c) export-share ACCESS comment level went to ic-chat. (d) The CSS section header took ic-document because the icon set has no code glyph - a borrowed-but-honest glyph, noted below. No decision opened: none of these change what the product does, only which picture names it.

Swept 206 occurrences across 59 files (58 pages + shared/components/entry.js, so the auto-injected history cards are covered), then re-ran shared/build-ds.mjs so the static bundle matches. Verified in a real browser, not by grep: all 89 pages loaded in 1280x900 iframes, 231 live edit-verb controls across 61 pages, every one ic-pencil with a mask actually in effect and a >=8px box; 91 surviving pen nibs, every one on a vector meaning (Pen tool, vector layer, text on a path, SVG). The runtime tooltip component rewrites title to data-tip, so the check had to match both - a title-only assertion reports a false zero. Standing audit-sweep clean: 89 pages, 75 segs, 80 dock managers, zero issues. Every touched page returns 200.

Left alone on purpose, with the reason: the redline arrow annotation layers (8 rows) and the "Arrow / annotate (P)" tool wear the pen nib. They are vector paths, so they do not collide with the edit verb, but a redline arrow reading as a nib is a separate legibility question on the focus surface - filed rather than folded in. Also wrote the rule into shared/AGENTS.md so the corpus stops re-deriving it: pencil is the edit verb, the nib is vector, and a glyph that looks nearly right for a second job means the second job needs its own icon.

ic-pencil is now the edit verb everywhere and the pen nib means vector only. 206 of the study's 304 nibs were standing in for an edit action, not the 179 the notes predicted: also 5 Rename buttons, 13 filmcard rows that spelled the same action 'Open' (retitled to Edit, since they are the identical component the app-shell exemplar labels Edit), 2 labelled Open buttons on capture cards, 'Edit main', the share-sheet edit access level, 2 editable-value carets, and a section header where the nib meant neither edit nor vector. Comment access took ic-chat. Swept 58 pages plus shared/components/entry.js so auto-injected history cards are covered, and rebuilt shared/dist. Verified in a browser, not by grep: 89 pages in 1280x900 iframes, 231 live edit-verb controls all ic-pencil with the mask actually in effect, 91 surviving nibs all on vector meanings, standing audit-sweep clean, every touched page 200. Rule recorded in shared/AGENTS.md. Audit at queue/audits/2026-08-23-edit-glyph.json with a screenshot. Redline arrow annotations still wear the nib on purpose, filed as redline-arrow-annotations-get-an-arrow-glyph-not.
